summary:
Albania does not criminalise consensual same-sex conduct or gender expression. The criminal code carried a ten-year prison sentence for homosexual conduct until 1995, and no equivalent provision has been reinstated.

The operative instrument is the comprehensive anti-discrimination law in force from 4 February 2010, which covers sexual orientation in employment, goods and services, education, housing and health care. In October 2020 it was expanded to prohibit discrimination on the grounds of sex characteristics and HIV status.

On 4 May 2013 the Albanian Parliament amended the criminal code to place hate crimes motivated by sexual orientation and gender identity on the same footing as offences motivated by race, ethnicity, religion and disability. In the same session it passed a law punishing dissemination of homophobic information through any means, including the internet, by a fine and up to two years' imprisonment.

Enforcement of the protection machinery has been uneven. In December 2010 the Deputy Commissioner for Labour, Social Affairs and Health, Tritan Shehu, said publicly that medical staff should treat homosexuality as a hormonal and psychological disorder. The Commissioner for Protection from Discrimination reprimanded him on 30 September 2011, after a lengthy delay and after LGBT groups had already lost trust in the body over slow, bureaucratically impeded investigations.

In 2016 members of parliament removed sexual orientation and gender identity from Article 18 of the Constitution at the last moment, under pressure from faith-based leaders and contrary to earlier promises. PINK Embassy condemned the removal on 20 July 2016.

Albania recognises neither marriage nor civil unions for same-sex couples in any form, and households headed by same-sex couples are not eligible for the legal protections available to different-sex households. A trans visitor whose relationship would be classified as same-sex under Albanian law has no route to formal recognition of the partnership.

Social attitudes discourage public expression of LGBT identity. In the 2010 Gallup Balkan Monitor survey, 56.1 per cent of Albanian respondents said homosexuals should not show their preferences in public, and 56.2 per cent said they should not hold public posts such as teacher. A 2022 nationwide questionnaire found that 9.3 per cent of Albanians would accept an LGBT person as a family doctor. In 2015, 55 per cent of Albanians aged 16 to 27 said they would not want homosexual neighbours, and a 2016 study found homophobia among Albanian university students associated with being male, politically conservative and religious.

The bias-motivated violence record available for trans people is a log kept by the group Rainbowphilia, which recorded ten cases during the year covered by ILGA-Europe's 2024 review. No general homicide rate for Albania appears in the source inventory, so these figures cannot be set against the background rate of violence in the country.

The UN Independent Expert on violence and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity visited Albania from 1 to 12 July 2024. The end-of-mission statement assessed good practices and challenges and issued recommendations to the state. The resulting report, A/HRC/59/43/Add.1 of 17 June 2025 by Graeme Reid, evaluates Albania's adherence to national and international human rights standards on sexual orientation and gender identity, drawing on information gathered before, during and after the visit.

In June 2016 the government adopted a National Action Plan for LGBTI addressing bullying and discrimination in primary and secondary education, which drew strong political opposition.

Complaints arising from screenings of the film 'Strange World' were mediated during the period covered by the 2024 review, with the Commissioner for Protection from Discrimination ruling in favour in one case.
tangentialFactors:
Opposition politicians have campaigned against LGBT material in schools. Democratic Party MP Luçiano Boçi described LGBT extra-curricular groups in high schools as having a suspicious, revolting agenda. In the same week, MP Nard Ndoka posted that the government was LGBT and was pushing LGBT values in schools. Both interventions came from the Berisha-led opposition.

The 2010 anti-discrimination law was framed by its supporters as driven by EU integration. In July 2009 Prime Minister Sali Berisha had voiced support for gay marriage, but the law as passed did not provide for it.
localsOnly:
Community organisations run support schemes for trans residents, including food packages for trans sex workers and for people living with HIV.

Pro LGBT launched the news portal historiaime.al in 2012, and the first Miss Trans Albania pageant was held in Tirana in 2014. Both are visibility projects rather than service provision.

Lodging a discrimination complaint rarely produces a timely outcome: only one of nine LGBT-linked cases had been concluded by December 2012, and the reprimand of the Deputy Commissioner for Labour, Social Affairs and Health came in September 2011, nine months after his remarks.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Albania operates a legal gender recognition procedure, and how identity documents record gender, is not established by this inventory. People's Advocate Erinda Ballanca pledged in April 2018 to support the right to change one's legal gender, but no operative procedure, eligibility condition or document-handling rule is described in the sources. A visitor who needs a marker or document change should treat the position as unresolved.

The ten bias-motivated violence cases logged by Rainbowphilia are a raw count from a community group's record. No general homicide rate for Albania appears in the inventory, so no comparison between trans-specific violence and the background rate can be made, and the figure cannot be read as a measure of severity.

Whether the 2013 offence of disseminating homophobic information has been applied in practice, and against whom, is not documented in the inventory, and the enforcement record of the hate-crime amendment beyond the mediated film complaints is not sourced.
